01-01.title: New Year
01-01.line: begin the year with Ardas and a hopeful heart.
01-01.meaning: many Sikhs visit the gurdwara on New Year's Day to start the year with prayer and kirtan.

01-02.title: Naam Japo
01-02.line: remember God's Name through the day.
01-02.meaning: one of the three pillars of Sikh life. a quiet "Waheguru" while you work counts.

01-03.title: Mool Mantar
01-03.original: ੴ ਸਤਿ ਨਾਮੁ ਕਰਤਾ ਪੁਰਖੁ ਨਿਰਭਉ ਨਿਰਵੈਰੁ ਅਕਾਲ ਮੂਰਤਿ ਅਜੂਨੀ ਸੈਭੰ ਗੁਰ ਪ੍ਰਸਾਦਿ ॥
01-03.line: one Creator, Truth by name, without fear, without hate, timeless.
01-03.meaning: the opening of the Guru Granth Sahib: everything Sikhs believe about God, in one breath.

01-04.title: Share a Meal
01-04.line: who could you share a meal with this week?
01-04.meaning: langar starts with one plate offered to one person.

01-05.title: The True Bargain
01-05.line: given money to trade, young Nanak fed hungry people instead.
01-05.meaning: he called it the true bargain, "sacha sauda". the best trade is kindness.

01-06.title: Chardi Kala
01-06.line: chardi kala: rising spirits, even in hard times.
01-06.meaning: a Sikh way of being: hopeful and resilient, whatever comes.

01-07.title: Truth Above All
01-07.line: truth is higher than everything, but higher still is truthful living.
01-07.meaning: Guru Nanak Dev Ji says it's not enough to know truth. live it.

01-08.title: Five Minutes
01-08.line: sit for five minutes with Waheguru in your heart.
01-08.meaning: a little simran, kept up daily, grows deep roots.

01-09.title: Bhai Mardana
01-09.line: Bhai Mardana Ji was Guru Nanak Dev Ji's lifelong companion.
01-09.meaning: a musician who walked every mile with the Guru. friendship is sacred.

01-10.title: Kirat Karo
01-10.meaning: the second pillar: work hard and honestly. your daily work can be part of your faith.

01-11.title: Harmandir Sahib
01-11.meaning: open on four sides, it serves free langar to many thousands every day.

01-12.title: Fear No One, Frighten No One
01-12.line: frighten no one, and be afraid of no one.
01-12.meaning: Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji's words for true freedom: gentle and brave at once.
01-12.source: Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji, Salok Mahalla 9

01-13.title: Bhagat Kabir Ji
01-13.line: a weaver whose songs fill many pages of the Guru.
01-13.meaning: Kabir Ji's hymns are part of the Guru Granth Sahib. the Gurus honored truth wherever they found it.

01-14.title: True in the Beginning
01-14.line: true before time began, true through the ages, true now.
01-14.meaning: the salok that opens Japji Sahib. whatever changes today, the True One doesn't.

01-15.title: Quiet Seva
01-15.line: do one helpful thing that no one will notice.
01-15.meaning: the best seva is done quietly. let it be your secret.

01-16.title: Vand Chhako
01-16.meaning: the third pillar: share with others, especially those in need. even a snack counts.

01-17.title: Bhai Lalo's Bread
01-17.line: Guru Nanak Dev Ji chose a carpenter's honest bread over a rich man's feast.
01-17.meaning: the story of Bhai Lalo and Malik Bhago: honest work is sweet.

01-18.title: Tera, Tera
01-18.line: weighing grain, Guru Nanak Dev Ji reached thirteen, "tera", and kept saying "Yours".
01-18.meaning: at the Sultanpur granary, the count turned into a prayer: everything is Yours.

01-19.title: Hukam
01-19.meaning: everything moves within the Creator's will. trust it a little more today.

01-20.title: One Father
01-20.original: ਏਕੁ ਪਿਤਾ ਏਕਸ ਕੇ ਹਮ ਬਾਰਿਕ
01-20.line: one is our father; we are all children of the One.
01-20.meaning: Guru Arjan Dev Ji reminds us we're one family. treat someone like a sibling today.

01-21.title: Write It Down
01-21.line: write one line of Gurbani on a note and keep it near.
01-21.meaning: carry the Guru's word through your day.

01-22.title: Baba Buddha Ji
01-22.line: Baba Buddha Ji served six Gurus over a long life.
01-22.meaning: he was the first granthi of the Harmandir Sahib. faithful service across generations.

01-23.title: Seva
01-23.line: serve others without expecting anything back.
01-23.meaning: seva is selfless service: washing dishes, cleaning shoes, helping a neighbor.

01-24.title: Pauri 1
01-24.original: ਸੋਚੈ ਸੋਚਿ ਨ ਹੋਵਈ ਜੇ ਸੋਚੀ ਲਖ ਵਾਰ ॥
01-24.line: thinking a hundred thousand times doesn't bring purity.
01-24.meaning: Guru Nanak Dev Ji says we can't think our way to peace. walking in the Creator's will does it.

01-25.title: Honest Work
01-25.line: do today's work as if the Guru were watching kindly.
01-25.meaning: kirat karo: honest effort, done well, is a prayer.

01-26.title: The Udasis
01-26.line: Guru Nanak Dev Ji walked thousands of miles to share his message.
01-26.meaning: his four great journeys, with Bhai Mardana, took him across Asia.

01-27.title: Simran
01-27.meaning: simran is meditation on the Name. a few slow breaths with "Waheguru" is enough.

01-28.title: Nadar
01-28.line: nadar: the Creator's glance of grace.
01-28.meaning: grace is freely given, Gurbani says. you are seen with kindness.

01-29.title: No Stranger
01-29.original: ਨਾ ਕੋ ਬੈਰੀ ਨਹੀ ਬਿਗਾਨਾ ਸਗਲ ਸੰਗਿ ਹਮ ਕਉ ਬਨਿ ਆਈ ॥
01-29.line: no one is my enemy, no one is a stranger; i get along with all.
01-29.meaning: Guru Arjan Dev Ji's line about seeing everyone as a friend.

01-30.title: Phone Down
01-30.line: put the phone down during a meal with others.
01-30.meaning: pangat means being fully present with whoever shares your food.

01-31.title: Langar
01-31.line: everyone sits together and eats the same meal.
01-31.meaning: the Guru's free kitchen feeds anyone, of any background. equality on a plate.

02-01.title: Walking in Hukam
02-01.original: ਹੁਕਮਿ ਰਜਾਈ ਚਲਣਾ ਨਾਨਕ ਲਿਖਿਆ ਨਾਲਿ ॥
02-01.line: walk in the Creator's will; it is written with us.
02-01.meaning: the answer to pauri 1's question: live in harmony with hukam, the divine order.

02-02.title: Bhai Gurdas
02-02.line: Bhai Gurdas Ji wrote down the first Granth for Guru Arjan Dev Ji.
02-02.meaning: his own poems are called "the key to Gurbani".

02-03.title: One Breath
02-03.meaning: a simple simran you can do anywhere, even in a queue.

02-04.title: Akal Takht
02-04.line: the throne of the Timeless One.
02-04.meaning: the highest seat of Sikh authority, facing the Harmandir Sahib.

02-05.title: Kartarpur
02-05.line: Guru Nanak Dev Ji spent his last years farming at Kartarpur.
02-05.meaning: he showed that a spiritual life and an honest working life go together.

02-06.title: Steady in Sorrow
02-06.line: the wise one is not shaken by pain or pleasure.
02-06.meaning: Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji describes a steady heart that stays the same in good and bad times.
02-06.source: Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji, Raag Sorath

02-07.title: Pangat
02-07.line: sit in a line, side by side, all equal.
02-07.meaning: in langar no one gets a better seat. try treating everyone today as equals.

02-08.title: Sehaj
02-08.meaning: a peaceful, steady state of mind. let one thing be easy today.

02-09.title: Baba Farid Ji
02-09.line: a Sufi poet of Punjab, honored in the Guru.
02-09.meaning: his saloks in the Guru Granth Sahib speak of humility and patience.

02-10.title: Pauri 2
02-10.line: everything is within hukam; nothing is outside it.
02-10.meaning: understanding the divine order, says Guru Nanak Dev Ji, quiets the ego.

02-11.title: Rising Spirits
02-11.line: find one reason for hope today.
02-11.meaning: chardi kala isn't pretending; it's looking for the light that's still there.

02-12.title: Sangat
02-12.meaning: the sangat is the community gathered in the Guru's presence. call a good friend today.

02-13.title: Embodiment of Light
02-13.original: ਮਨ ਤੂੰ ਜੋਤਿ ਸਰੂਪੁ ਹੈ ਆਪਣਾ ਮੂਲੁ ਪਛਾਣੁ ॥
02-13.line: O mind, you are the embodiment of light: know your origin.
02-13.meaning: Guru Amar Das Ji reminds us that we come from divine light. remember that today.

02-14.title: Give Before Asking
02-14.line: give something before you ask for anything today.
02-14.meaning: the Guru's house teaches giving first.

02-15.title: Bhai Kanhaiya
02-15.line: Bhai Kanhaiya Ji gave water to wounded soldiers on both sides.
02-15.meaning: Guru Gobind Singh Ji praised him and gave him ointment too. kindness without borders.

02-16.title: Mardana's Rabab
02-16.line: Bhai Mardana played; Guru Nanak Dev Ji sang.
02-16.meaning: the first Sikh kirtan came from a friendship of music and faith.

02-17.title: The Bowl of Milk
02-17.line: a full bowl of milk, and a jasmine petal floating on top.
02-17.meaning: told the city was already full of holy men, Guru Nanak Dev Ji answered that he would rest lightly on top, like the petal.

02-18.title: Sat
02-18.meaning: the first of five virtues. truth spoken kindly.

02-19.title: Amrit Vela
02-19.meaning: the quiet hours before dawn are treasured for prayer. if not dawn, any quiet minute works.

02-20.title: Pauri 3
02-20.line: the Giver keeps giving; we grow tired of receiving.
02-20.meaning: some sing of God's power, some of God's gifts. the gifts never stop.

02-21.title: Everyone Equal
02-21.line: treat the next person you meet as an equal.
02-21.meaning: in Sikhi there are no ranks before the Guru.

02-22.title: Nitnem
02-22.meaning: Nitnem is a daily rhythm of banis. even one, read slowly, keeps the rhythm alive.

02-23.title: Bhai Lehna's Service
02-23.line: Bhai Lehna served so humbly that he became the second Guru.
02-23.meaning: Guru Nanak Dev Ji named him Angad, "part of my own body".

02-24.title: Earn and Share
02-24.line: one who earns by honest work and gives some away knows the path.
02-24.meaning: Guru Nanak Dev Ji's simple formula: work hard, then share.

02-25.title: Patience
02-25.line: be patient with one person who tests you.
02-25.meaning: Japji Sahib calls patience the goldsmith of a good life.

02-26.title: Bhai Nand Lal
02-26.line: Bhai Nand Lal Ji was a poet in Guru Gobind Singh Ji's court.
02-26.meaning: he wrote beautiful verse about love for the Guru.

02-27.title: Takht Kesgarh Sahib
02-27.line: Anandpur Sahib, birthplace of the Khalsa.
02-27.meaning: where Guru Gobind Singh Ji created the Khalsa on Vaisakhi, 1699.

02-28.title: Santokh
02-28.meaning: happiness with what we have. notice three good things you already have.

02-29.title: An Extra Day
02-29.line: an extra day: spend it on seva.
02-29.meaning: a day that comes once in four years is a lovely gift to give away.

03-01.title: Pauri 4
03-01.line: in the early hours before dawn, reflect on true greatness.
03-01.meaning: amrit vela, the ambrosial hours, is the time Sikhs rise to remember Waheguru.

03-02.title: Japji Sahib
03-02.line: the morning prayer of Guru Nanak Dev Ji.
03-02.meaning: Japji Sahib opens the Guru Granth Sahib and many Sikh mornings.

03-03.title: Good Company
03-03.line: spend a moment with people who lift you up.
03-03.meaning: sangat shapes us. choose it well.

03-04.title: Let Go of Pride
03-04.line: O saints, give up the pride of the mind.
03-04.meaning: Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji's gentle advice: pride makes us suffer. let some go today.
03-04.source: Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji, Raag Gauri

03-05.title: Bhagat Ravidas Ji
03-05.line: a leatherworker who sang of a city without sorrow.
03-05.meaning: Ravidas Ji dreamed of "Begampura", a place with no pain and no ranks.

03-06.title: Guru Angad's Script
03-06.line: Guru Angad Dev Ji gave Punjabi a script for everyone.
03-06.meaning: he shaped Gurmukhi and taught children to read it.

03-07.title: Rehras Sahib
03-07.line: the evening prayer at the end of work.
03-07.meaning: Rehras Sahib is recited at dusk. a lovely way to close the working day.

03-08.title: Pauri 5
03-08.line: sing, listen, and keep love in your heart.
03-08.meaning: Waheguru can't be set up or made by us. we simply sing, listen and love.

03-09.title: The Light in All
03-09.line: in everyone is the light, and that light is the One.
03-09.meaning: from the evening prayer Kirtan Sohila: everyone shines with the same light.

03-10.title: Rest Day
03-10.line: rest is also a gift from Waheguru.
03-10.meaning: chardi kala includes looking after yourself. a calm day is good too.

03-11.title: Daya
03-11.meaning: Japji Sahib says dharma is the child of compassion. start there.

03-12.title: Stand Up
03-12.line: speak up kindly for someone who is left out.
03-12.meaning: the Gurus stood with the powerless. a small stand counts.

03-13.title: Mai Bhago
03-13.line: Mai Bhago Ji inspired forty men to return and stand firm.
03-13.meaning: a brave woman who led by example. courage has no gender.

03-14.title: Kirtan Sohila
03-14.meaning: Kirtan Sohila is said before sleep, putting the day in Waheguru's hands.

03-15.title: Healthy Bodies
03-15.line: Guru Angad Dev Ji encouraged wrestling and exercise.
03-15.meaning: he cared for the young in body and spirit alike.

03-16.title: Pauri 6
03-16.line: hear even one teaching of the Guru, and the mind fills with jewels.
03-16.meaning: one line, truly heard, is treasure. maybe today's card is yours.

03-17.title: Ardas
03-17.line: a standing prayer of hope and thanks.
03-17.meaning: Ardas closes most Sikh gatherings. it remembers the past and asks blessings for all.

03-18.title: Duni Chand's Needle
03-18.line: keep this needle for me, and give it back in the next world.
03-18.meaning: a rich man realized he could take nothing with him, and began sharing his wealth.

03-19.title: A Tenth
03-19.line: what could you give a little of today: time, money, attention?

03-20.title: Nimrata
03-20.meaning: the Gurus taught that the humble are lifted up. let someone else go first today.

03-21.title: The Sky as a Tray
03-21.line: the sky is the tray, the sun and moon its lamps.
03-21.meaning: Guru Nanak Dev Ji's aarti: all of nature is already worshipping. look up tonight.

03-22.title: Hard Day
03-22.line: on a hard day, say Ardas, then take one small step.
03-22.meaning: the Gurus faced great hardship with trust and courage.

03-23.title: Takht Damdama Sahib
03-23.line: Talwandi Sabo, the Guru's city of learning.
03-23.meaning: where Guru Gobind Singh Ji completed the final version of the Guru Granth Sahib.

03-24.title: Hukamnama
03-24.line: the Guru's word for the day.
03-24.meaning: each day a random page of the Guru Granth Sahib is opened and read as guidance.

03-25.title: The Forty Liberated Ones
03-25.line: forty who had left came back, and were forgiven.
03-25.meaning: at Muktsar, the Guru tore up their letter of leaving. it's never too late to return.

03-26.title: Mata Khivi's Kitchen
03-26.line: Mata Khivi Ji ran the langar with warmth.
03-26.meaning: Guru Granth Sahib praises her generous kitchen. hospitality is holy.

03-27.title: Pauri 7
03-27.line: the One gives goodness even to those who have none.
03-27.meaning: long life and fame mean little without grace. and grace is given freely.

03-28.title: Remembering
03-28.line: remembering God is higher than all.
03-28.meaning: from the first ashtpadi of Sukhmani Sahib. one remembered moment today counts.
03-28.source: Sukhmani Sahib, ashtpadi 1, Guru Arjan Dev Ji

03-29.title: Bhagat Namdev Ji
03-29.meaning: his songs of love for God are in the Guru Granth Sahib.

03-30.title: Gratitude
03-30.line: thank Waheguru for three ordinary things.
03-30.meaning: a roof, a meal, a friend. shukar, gratitude, is a Sikh habit.

03-31.title: Kirtan
03-31.meaning: kirtan fills the gurdwara with shabads. hum one today.

04-01.title: Pyaar
04-01.meaning: love of Waheguru, and of all creation. who can you show love to today?

04-02.title: Sweetness and Humility
04-02.original: ਮਿਠਤੁ ਨੀਵੀ ਨਾਨਕਾ ਗੁਣ ਚੰਗਿਆਈਆ ਤਤੁ ॥
04-02.line: sweetness and humility are the essence of all goodness.
04-02.meaning: Guru Nanak Dev Ji says these two qualities hold all the others.

04-03.title: Sweet Speech
04-03.line: say one sweet thing to someone at home.
04-03.meaning: Gurbani says sweetness and humility are the essence of goodness.

04-04.title: Karah Prashad
04-04.meaning: karah prashad is given to everyone in the gurdwara, received with cupped hands.

04-05.title: Pauri 8
04-05.line: by listening, sorrow and wrongdoing fall away.
04-05.meaning: the first of four "suniai" pauris on the power of deep listening. listen to one shabad today.

04-06.title: Water at Dawn
04-06.line: Guru Amar Das Ji carried water for his Guru every day.
04-06.meaning: he began serving in his sixties. it's never too late to begin.

04-07.title: Bhai Mati Das
04-07.line: Bhai Mati Das Ji stayed calm and kept praying to the end.
04-07.meaning: he stood with Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji in Delhi. faith steadier than fear.

04-08.title: Listening
04-08.line: listen fully to one person today.
04-08.meaning: Japji Sahib praises listening four times over. it's a gift you can give.

04-09.title: Covering the Head
04-09.line: cover your head as a sign of respect.
04-09.meaning: everyone covers their head in the gurdwara. it's a simple act of reverence.

04-10.title: Kaam
04-10.meaning: one of five "thieves" that steal our peace. notice when wanting takes over.

04-11.title: Pauri 9
04-11.line: by listening, even the ordinary become worthy of praise.
04-11.meaning: deep listening lifts anyone. no special status needed.

04-12.title: Takht Patna Sahib
04-12.line: the birthplace of Guru Gobind Singh Ji.
04-12.meaning: in Patna, Bihar, on the banks of the Ganga.

04-13.title: Sour Words
04-13.line: speaking harshly makes body and mind sour.
04-13.meaning: Guru Nanak Dev Ji says harsh words hurt the speaker too. choose sweet ones.

04-14.title: Work With Care
04-14.line: do one task today with full attention, as seva.
04-14.meaning: kirat and seva meet when work is done with love.

04-15.title: First Pangat
04-15.line: Guru Amar Das Ji asked all visitors to eat in langar first.
04-15.meaning: emperor or laborer, everyone sat together on the floor.

04-16.title: Shoes Off
04-16.line: remove your shoes and wash your hands before entering.
04-16.meaning: everyone enters the darbar the same way: humble and clean.

04-17.title: Soft Words
04-17.line: choose the sweet word over the sharp one.
04-17.meaning: Gurbani says harsh speech sours the speaker too.

04-18.title: Sajjan
04-18.line: Sajjan looked like a good host, but robbed his guests.
04-18.meaning: hearing Guru Nanak Dev Ji's shabad, he changed, and his inn became a place of welcome.

04-19.title: Bhai Jaita
04-19.line: Bhai Jaita Ji carried the Guru's head home to Anandpur.
04-19.meaning: a brave act of love. Guru Gobind Singh Ji embraced him as "the Guru's own son".

04-20.title: The Lotus
04-20.line: the one who knows God stays untouched, like a lotus in water.
04-20.meaning: Sukhmani Sahib describes the wise as living in the world without being stained by it.
04-20.source: Sukhmani Sahib, ashtpadi 8, Guru Arjan Dev Ji

04-21.title: The Five Ks
04-21.line: five articles of faith worn by initiated Sikhs.
04-21.meaning: kesh, kangha, kara, kachera and kirpan: each one a reminder of a Sikh promise.

04-22.title: Krodh
04-22.meaning: a thief of peace. when it rises, take a breath before you speak.

04-23.title: Bhagat Dhanna Ji
04-23.line: a farmer whose simple faith is honored.
04-23.meaning: Dhanna Ji's hymns ask for simple things: food, a home, a good life.

04-24.title: Pauri 10
04-24.line: by listening come truth, contentment and wisdom.
04-24.meaning: three gifts that arrive through attention. who can you really listen to today?

04-25.title: The Baoli
04-25.line: Guru Amar Das Ji built a stepwell at Goindwal.
04-25.meaning: clean water for everyone, of any background. care made practical.

04-26.title: Begin Again
04-26.line: if today went off course, begin again with Ardas.
04-26.meaning: the Guru always welcomes us back.

04-27.title: Kesh
04-27.line: uncut hair, kept as the Creator made it.
04-27.meaning: kesh is a sign of accepting the body as a gift, cared for with love.

04-28.title: Honoring Women
04-28.line: why call her lesser, from whom kings are born?
04-28.meaning: Guru Nanak Dev Ji honored women in the 1500s with this line. honor the women in your life.

04-29.title: See the Need
04-29.line: notice who around you needs help, and offer it.
04-29.meaning: the Gurus always noticed the hungry, the sick and the left-out.

04-30.title: Bhai Mani Singh
04-30.line: Bhai Mani Singh Ji cared for the Harmandir Sahib and scripture.
04-30.meaning: a scholar and caretaker remembered for his unshakable faith.

05-01.title: Lobh
05-01.meaning: always wanting more. contentment, santokh, is its cure.

05-02.title: Pauri 11
05-02.line: by listening, one dives into the ocean of virtue.
05-02.meaning: each "suniai" pauri ends: the devotees blossom forever. listening makes us bloom.

05-03.title: Kangha
05-03.meaning: the kangha reminds Sikhs to keep tidy in body and in mind.

05-04.title: Nature
05-04.line: step outside and greet the air, water and earth.
05-04.meaning: Japji Sahib calls them guru, father and mother.

05-05.title: Founding Amritsar
05-05.line: Guru Ram Das Ji founded the city that became Amritsar.
05-05.meaning: he invited traders and craftspeople to build a city around the sacred pool.

05-06.title: Takht Hazur Sahib
05-06.line: Nanded, where the Guru Granth Sahib became Guru.
05-06.meaning: Guru Gobind Singh Ji spent his last days there.

05-07.title: Kara
05-07.line: a steel bracelet, with no beginning and no end.
05-07.meaning: the kara reminds the hand to do good, and of the One without end.

05-08.title: Medicine and Illness
05-08.line: sometimes pain becomes the medicine, and comfort the illness.
05-08.meaning: Guru Nanak Dev Ji says hard times can bring us closer to Waheguru.

05-09.title: Shukar
05-09.meaning: gratitude, said simply, softens the whole day.

05-10.title: Pauri 12
05-10.line: the state of the one who trusts can't be described.
05-10.meaning: the "mannai" pauris begin: faith that is lived, not just spoken.

05-11.title: Moh
05-11.meaning: love that grips too tight. hold things and people with an open hand.

05-12.title: Kachera
05-12.line: cotton undershorts, a sign of self-control.
05-12.meaning: the kachera is a reminder of modesty and self-respect.

05-13.title: Baba Deep Singh
05-13.line: Baba Deep Singh Ji was a scholar who copied the Guru Granth Sahib by hand.
05-13.meaning: he served at Damdama Sahib and gave his all to protect the Harmandir Sahib.

05-14.title: Courage
05-14.line: what is one brave, good thing you could do today?
05-14.meaning: saint and soldier: gentle heart, brave hands.

05-15.title: The Wedding Hymns
05-15.line: Guru Ram Das Ji wrote the four lavan.
05-15.meaning: Sikh couples still marry to his words.

05-16.title: One Human Race
05-16.meaning: Guru Gobind Singh Ji's famous line: no one is above or below anyone.
05-16.source: Guru Gobind Singh Ji, Akal Ustat, Dasam Granth

05-17.title: Bhagat Sain Ji
05-17.line: a barber whose devotion is in the Guru.
05-17.meaning: Sain Ji's hymn is an aarti of love. every trade can be holy.

05-18.title: Two Villages
05-18.line: to the rude village: stay here; to the kind one: scatter.
05-18.meaning: Guru Nanak Dev Ji wanted kindness spread everywhere, and unkindness kept in one place.

05-19.title: Kirpan
05-19.line: a small sword, a promise to protect.
05-19.meaning: the kirpan stands for courage and defending the weak, never for aggression.

05-20.title: Pauri 13
05-20.line: by trusting, the mind gains awareness and understanding.
05-20.meaning: faith opens the eyes, says Guru Nanak Dev Ji. trust brings clarity.

05-21.title: Dwelling in Nature
05-21.line: i am a sacrifice to Your creation, where You dwell.
05-21.meaning: Guru Nanak Dev Ji saw the Creator living inside the creation. notice it outside today.

05-22.title: Clean Heart
05-22.line: let one grudge go before sleeping.
05-22.meaning: a clean heart rests better than a clean house.

05-23.title: Ahankar
05-23.meaning: the thief that says "i did it all". humility, nimrata, sets us free.

05-24.title: Letting Go
05-24.line: which worry can you hand over to Waheguru?
05-24.meaning: bhana is trusting the Creator with what we can't control.

05-25.title: Compiling the Granth
05-25.line: Guru Arjan Dev Ji gathered the Gurus' words into one book.
05-25.meaning: in 1604 he installed it at the Harmandir Sahib, including saints of many backgrounds.

05-26.title: Dastar
05-26.line: the turban, worn with pride and responsibility.
05-26.meaning: the dastar signals that the wearer stands up for others. tying it is its own small practice.

05-27.title: Bhai Taru Singh
05-27.line: Bhai Taru Singh Ji fed travelers from his own small farm.
05-27.meaning: he chose to keep his faith over his own safety. kindness and courage together.

05-28.title: Pauri 14
05-28.line: the path of the one who trusts is never blocked.
05-28.meaning: when we walk with faith, the way opens. take the next small step.

05-29.title: Nankana Sahib
05-29.line: the birthplace of Guru Nanak Dev Ji.
05-29.meaning: pilgrims travel there for Guru Nanak Dev Ji's gurpurab.

05-30.title: Sarbat da Bhala
05-30.line: pray for the good of all.
05-30.meaning: every Ardas ends asking blessings for everyone, not just Sikhs. pray for a stranger today.

05-31.title: Simple Living
05-31.line: what could you do without today, and share instead?

06-01.title: Haumai
06-01.meaning: Gurbani calls it a deep illness, with its cure inside us. serve someone today.

06-02.title: Wonder
06-02.line: wondrous is the sound, wondrous the knowledge.
06-02.meaning: Guru Nanak Dev Ji's "vismaad": a hymn of pure wonder at everything.

06-03.title: Kind to Yourself
06-03.line: speak to yourself as the Guru would: kindly.
06-03.meaning: Gurbani says you are the embodiment of light. treat yourself that way.

06-04.title: Building the Harmandir
06-04.line: Guru Arjan Dev Ji built the Harmandir Sahib low, with four doors.
06-04.meaning: low so all must step down in humility; four doors so all are welcome.

06-05.title: Daswandh
06-05.line: share a tenth of what you earn.
06-05.meaning: many Sikhs give a tenth of their income or time to help others. any amount is a start.

06-06.title: Pauri 15
06-06.line: the one who trusts finds the door of freedom, and lifts their family too.
06-06.meaning: your faith blesses the people around you. it's never only for yourself.

06-07.title: Banda Singh Bahadur
06-07.line: Banda Singh Bahadur gave land to the people who farmed it.
06-07.meaning: a hermit who became a leader for the poor after meeting Guru Gobind Singh Ji.

06-08.title: Never Turn from Good
06-08.line: grant me this: may i never turn away from doing good.
06-08.meaning: Guru Gobind Singh Ji's prayer for courage to keep doing the right thing.
06-08.source: Guru Gobind Singh Ji, Chandi Charitar, Dasam Granth

06-09.title: Bhagat Pipa Ji
06-09.line: a king who gave up his throne to seek God.
06-09.meaning: Pipa Ji found everything in the body itself.

06-10.title: Humility
06-10.line: let someone else have the credit today.
06-10.meaning: nimrata, humility, is the Guru's favorite quality.

06-11.title: Gutka
06-11.line: a small prayer book, handled with care.
06-11.meaning: Sikhs wrap their gutka in cloth and keep it clean. the words are treated as precious.

06-12.title: Gurmukh
06-12.line: gurmukh: one whose face is turned to the Guru.
06-12.meaning: someone guided by the Guru's wisdom, not by ego. every day is a chance to turn.

06-13.title: Guru Arjan's Peace
06-13.line: in the hardest suffering, Guru Arjan Dev Ji said "Your will is sweet".
06-13.meaning: the first Sikh martyr met cruelty with calm trust.

06-14.title: The Long Illness
06-14.line: ego is a long illness, but its cure lies within it too.
06-14.meaning: Guru Angad Dev Ji says the cure for ego is found in the same place: within us.

06-15.title: Open Door
06-15.meaning: every gurdwara's door is open. let yours be open too.

06-16.title: Pauri 16
06-16.line: dharma, born of compassion, holds the world together with patience.
06-16.meaning: Guru Nanak Dev Ji says what holds up the earth is righteousness, the child of compassion.

06-17.title: Gurdwara
06-17.line: the door to the Guru, open to all.
06-17.meaning: every gurdwara welcomes anyone, for prayer, rest or a free meal.

06-18.title: The Emperor in the Pangat
06-18.line: an emperor sat on the floor to eat langar before meeting the Guru.
06-18.meaning: at Goindwal, everyone ate together first, whoever they were.

06-19.title: The Light in Others
06-19.line: look for the Guru's light in someone who annoys you.
06-19.meaning: Gurbani says the same light is in all. even them.

06-20.title: Bhai Bidhi Chand
06-20.line: Bhai Bidhi Chand Ji was bold, clever and devoted.
06-20.meaning: a beloved Sikh of Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji, remembered for brave and witty deeds.

06-21.title: Kartarpur Sahib
06-21.line: where Guru Nanak Dev Ji farmed and taught.
06-21.meaning: a place of honest work, shared meals and prayer.

06-22.title: Nishan Sahib
06-22.line: the flag that says: here is shelter.
06-22.meaning: the Nishan Sahib flies above every gurdwara so travelers know where to find food and rest.

06-23.title: Manmukh
06-23.line: manmukh: one led by the restless mind.
06-23.meaning: we all have manmukh moments. noticing is the first step back.

06-24.title: Two Swords
06-24.line: Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji wore two swords: miri and piri.
06-24.meaning: one for worldly duty, one for spirit, held in balance.

06-25.title: Pauri 17
06-25.line: countless ways to worship; whatever pleases You is good.
06-25.meaning: there are endless ways to love the Creator. yours is welcome.

06-26.title: Highest Dharma
06-26.line: of all practices, the highest is to remember the Name.
06-26.meaning: Guru Arjan Dev Ji in Sukhmani Sahib: remembering Waheguru is the purest deed.

06-27.title: A Small Gift
06-27.line: give a small gift for no reason.
06-27.meaning: generosity without a reason is the Guru's way.

06-28.title: Four Doors
06-28.line: the Harmandir Sahib has doors on all four sides.
06-28.meaning: open to people from every direction and background. no one is turned away.

06-29.title: Morning Word
06-29.line: read one line of Gurbani before your phone.
06-29.meaning: start the day with the Guru's voice first.

06-30.title: Pauri 19
06-30.line: through the Word come knowledge, song and praise.
06-30.meaning: the Shabad is how we know, sing and praise. it shapes everything.

07-01.title: Only Love
07-01.line: those who love, only they find the Beloved.
07-01.meaning: Guru Gobind Singh Ji: love, not rituals, is the way to Waheguru.
07-01.source: Guru Gobind Singh Ji, Tav Prasad Savaiye, Dasam Granth

07-02.title: Path
07-02.line: reading Gurbani from start to finish.
07-02.meaning: an Akhand Path is a continuous reading over about two days, often for family occasions.

07-03.title: Naam
07-03.line: naam: the divine Name and presence.
07-03.meaning: more than a word: the presence of the Creator in everything.

07-04.title: The Akal Takht
07-04.line: Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji built the Akal Takht in 1606.
07-04.meaning: the "throne of the Timeless One" stands facing the Harmandir Sahib.

07-05.title: Makhan Shah
07-05.line: a sailor prayed in a storm and kept his promise.
07-05.meaning: Makhan Shah Lubana kept his word, and found Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji. keep a promise today.

07-06.title: Bhagat Trilochan Ji
07-06.line: a saint who wrote about what fills our mind at the end.
07-06.meaning: Trilochan Ji reminds us that what we think about shapes us.

07-07.title: A Thank-You
07-07.line: thank someone who serves you: a cook, a driver, a cleaner.
07-07.meaning: every bit of work is honorable in Sikhi.

07-08.title: Sehaj Path
07-08.line: reading the Guru Granth Sahib at your own pace.
07-08.meaning: a gentle, unhurried reading, a page or two at a time. no rush.

07-09.title: Sukhmani
07-09.line: the Name of God is the jewel of peace, sweet as nectar.
07-09.meaning: the refrain of Sukhmani Sahib, the "pearl of peace". many read it in hard times.

07-10.title: Stand Tall
07-10.line: stand tall in who you are today.
07-10.meaning: Sikhs keep their identity with quiet pride and kindness.

07-11.title: Pauri 20
07-11.line: water washes dirty hands; the Name washes a stained mind.
07-11.meaning: just as soap cleans clothes, remembering Waheguru cleans the heart.

07-12.title: The Fifty-Two Kings
07-12.line: Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji refused freedom unless 52 kings came too.
07-12.meaning: they each held a tassel of his cloak and walked out together. Bandi Chhor Divas remembers it.

07-13.title: Shabad
07-13.meaning: each hymn in the Guru Granth Sahib is a shabad. the Word itself is the Guru.

07-14.title: Shoe Seva
07-14.line: cleaning the shoes of the sangat.
07-14.meaning: among the humblest and most honored kinds of seva at the gurdwara.

07-15.title: Goindwal Sahib
07-15.line: home of Guru Amar Das Ji's stepwell.
07-15.meaning: pilgrims recite Japji Sahib on each of its 84 steps.

07-16.title: Bhai Ghanaiya's Ointment
07-16.line: the Guru said: give water, and give healing too.
07-16.meaning: Bhai Kanhaiya Ji's seva grew into a legacy of care for everyone in need.

07-17.title: Forgiveness
07-17.meaning: Baba Farid Ji says answer wrong with good.

07-18.title: Bhai Manjh's Firewood
07-18.line: fallen into a well, Bhai Manjh held the langar wood above the water.
07-18.meaning: his first thought was keeping the Guru's kitchen supplied. devotion in a crisis.

07-19.title: Jora Ghar
07-19.line: the place where shoes are kept.
07-19.meaning: volunteers look after everyone's shoes, kings and laborers alike.

07-20.title: We Reap What We Sow
07-20.line: we plant the seed, and we eat its fruit.
07-20.meaning: Guru Nanak Dev Ji's simple line on actions and their results. plant something good today.

07-21.title: Sweet Will
07-21.line: how sweet Your will seems to me.
07-21.meaning: Guru Arjan Dev Ji's line of acceptance, said even in suffering. a deep trust.

07-22.title: Unity
07-22.line: find something in common with someone different from you.
07-22.meaning: One Creator, one human family. look for the common thread.

07-23.title: The Flower
07-23.line: Guru Har Rai Sahib Ji was sad when his robe broke a flower.
07-23.meaning: he learned to move gently through the world. walk softly today.

07-24.title: Bani
07-24.meaning: Gurbani is the Guru's word. reading it is like sitting with the Guru.

07-25.title: Prakash and Sukhasan
07-25.line: the Guru is opened at dawn and rested at night.
07-25.meaning: the Guru Granth Sahib is treated as a living Guru, honored each morning and evening.

07-26.title: Hydrate a Stranger
07-26.line: offer water or a kind word to someone in need.
07-26.meaning: chhabeel, free drinks for passers-by, is a loved form of seva.

07-27.title: The Mist Cleared
07-27.line: the true Guru Nanak appeared, the mist cleared and light spread.
07-27.meaning: Bhai Gurdas Ji's joyful description of Guru Nanak Dev Ji coming into the world.

07-28.title: Bhagat Beni Ji
07-28.line: a saint of deep inner practice.
07-28.meaning: Beni Ji's hymns in the Guru Granth Sahib speak of the inward path.

07-29.title: Bhagat Puran Singh
07-29.line: Bhagat Puran Singh carried a disabled boy on his back for years.
07-29.meaning: he founded Pingalwara in Amritsar, a home for the sick and abandoned.

07-30.title: Pauri 21
07-30.line: when was the world made? only the Creator knows.
07-30.meaning: not even scholars can name the day. it's okay not to know everything.

07-31.title: Chaur Sahib
07-31.line: waving the chaur as a sign of honor.
07-31.meaning: a sign of respect for the Guru Granth Sahib, as for royalty.

08-01.title: The Garden and the Healer
08-01.line: Guru Har Rai Sahib Ji kept gardens and gave medicine to all.
08-01.meaning: he cared for animals, plants and the sick. care for something living today.

08-02.title: The Whole World Hurts
08-02.line: Nanak, the whole world is in some pain.
08-02.meaning: everyone carries something. be gentle with the people you meet today.

08-03.title: Morning Ardas
08-03.line: start the day with a short Ardas.
08-03.meaning: ask for strength, give thanks, and pray for everyone.

08-04.title: Sikh
08-04.meaning: being a Sikh means always being a student. you're learning right now.

08-05.title: Feed Someone
08-05.line: buy or cook a little extra and give it away.
08-05.meaning: the Guru's kitchen never closes. your kitchen can open a little.

08-06.title: Anand Karaj
08-06.meaning: a Sikh wedding: the couple walks around the Guru Granth Sahib four times as the lavan are sung.

08-07.title: Khadur Sahib
08-07.line: where Guru Angad Dev Ji lived and taught.
08-07.meaning: a quiet town where the Gurmukhi script was nurtured.

08-08.title: Pauri 22
08-08.line: worlds beyond worlds, skies beyond skies: no one can count them.
08-08.meaning: Guru Nanak Dev Ji wrote of countless worlds long before telescopes. wonder is part of faith.

08-09.title: The Sahibzade
08-09.line: the four sons of Guru Gobind Singh Ji were remembered for courage.
08-09.meaning: two elder sons fell at Chamkaur; the two youngest kept their faith at Sirhind.

08-10.title: Naming a Child
08-10.line: a name chosen from the Guru's word.
08-10.meaning: the hukamnama's first letter often guides a baby's name. every child begins with the Guru.

08-11.title: The Child Guru
08-11.line: Guru Har Krishan Sahib Ji became Guru at five.
08-11.meaning: in Delhi he cared for people sick with smallpox. Gurdwara Bangla Sahib stands there now.

08-12.title: Name Before Sleep
08-12.meaning: let the last word of your day be gratitude.

08-13.title: Guru
08-13.line: guru: the one who brings light into darkness.
08-13.meaning: Sikhs have ten human Gurus and the eternal Guru Granth Sahib.

08-14.title: One Light
08-14.line: first, God created the light; from it came all beings.
08-14.meaning: Bhagat Kabir Ji: if everyone comes from one light, who is good and who is bad?

08-15.title: Evening Peace
08-15.line: close the day with a quiet "Waheguru".
08-15.meaning: let the day rest in the Guru's hands.

08-16.title: Pauri 23
08-16.line: rivers pour into the ocean without knowing its depth.
08-16.meaning: we praise the Creator without grasping how vast Waheguru is. that's fine.

08-17.title: Kaur and Singh
08-17.line: every Sikh woman is a princess, every man a lion.
08-17.meaning: Guru Gobind Singh Ji gave the names Kaur and Singh, so no one is judged by family name.

08-18.title: Soft Hands
08-18.line: the Guru asked a young man why his hands had never done seva.
08-18.meaning: Guru Gobind Singh Ji taught that helping hands are holy hands.

08-19.title: Chardi Kala
08-19.original: ਨਾਨਕ ਨਾਮ ਚੜ੍ਹਦੀ ਕਲਾ ਤੇਰੇ ਭਾਣੇ ਸਰਬੱਤ ਦਾ ਭਲਾ
08-19.line: Nanak, with the Name comes rising spirits; by Your will, may all be well.
08-19.meaning: the closing words of Ardas, said by Sikhs every day: optimism, and blessings for everyone.

08-20.title: Bhagat Jaidev Ji
08-20.line: a Sanskrit poet from Bengal, honored in the Guru.
08-20.meaning: Jaidev Ji's words show the Gurus gathered wisdom from far and wide.

08-21.title: Bangla Sahib's Water
08-21.line: Guru Har Krishan Sahib Ji gave water and comfort to the sick.
08-21.meaning: the sarovar at Bangla Sahib is still visited by many seeking peace.

08-22.title: A Learner Today
08-22.line: learn one new thing about Sikhi today.
08-22.meaning: Sikh means learner. curiosity is part of the path.

08-23.title: Baba Ajit Singh
08-23.line: Sahibzada Ajit Singh Ji faced the battle at Chamkaur bravely.
08-23.meaning: the eldest son of Guru Gobind Singh Ji, remembered for courage and devotion.

08-24.title: Amrit Sanchar
08-24.meaning: Sikhs who are ready take amrit and commit to a disciplined, giving life.

08-25.title: Khalsa
08-25.meaning: the community of initiated Sikhs founded in 1699, committed to justice and devotion.

08-26.title: Pauri 24
08-26.line: there is no end to praise, no end to giving.
08-26.meaning: whatever we say about Waheguru, there's always more. limitless.

08-27.title: Under the Guru's Shelter
08-27.line: not even a hot wind can touch one in the Creator's shelter.
08-27.meaning: Guru Arjan Dev Ji's comfort for anxious days.

08-28.title: Learn a Shabad
08-28.line: learn the first line of a shabad by heart.
08-28.meaning: a memorized line can comfort you anywhere.

08-29.title: Panj Pyare
08-29.meaning: five who offered their heads to Guru Gobind Singh Ji in 1699. they still lead Sikh ceremonies.

08-30.title: Tarn Taran Sahib
08-30.line: founded by Guru Arjan Dev Ji.
08-30.meaning: it has one of the largest sarovars, and Guru Arjan Dev Ji cared for the sick there.

08-31.title: Baba Bakale
08-31.line: a trader found Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji quietly in prayer at Bakala.
08-31.meaning: Makhan Shah Lubana searched past the loud claimants and found the true Guru.

09-01.title: Kind Eyes
09-01.line: look at everyone today as family.
09-01.meaning: One father, many children. Gurbani says we're all related.

09-02.title: Gatka
09-02.meaning: gatka is practiced with sticks and swords at festivals, a celebration of discipline and readiness.

09-03.title: Pauri 25
09-03.line: the gifts are so many, they cannot be written down.
09-03.meaning: even the hard days, Guru Nanak Dev Ji says, can carry a hidden gift.

09-04.title: Sangat and Pangat
09-04.meaning: two words that sum up Sikh community: shared prayer and shared food.

09-05.title: Baba Zorawar and Fateh Singh
09-05.line: two little brothers held to their faith and didn't give in.
09-05.meaning: the younger Sahibzade, aged around nine and six, are honored for faith beyond their years.

09-06.title: Farid: Answer with Good
09-06.line: do good to those who do you wrong; don't let anger in.
09-06.meaning: Baba Farid Ji's advice for a calm heart. try it with one small hurt today.

09-07.title: Help at Home
09-07.line: do a chore at home before someone asks.
09-07.meaning: seva begins with the people closest to us.

09-08.title: Sant-Sipahi
09-08.meaning: the Sikh ideal: a peaceful heart and the courage to defend others.

09-09.title: Walk Gently
09-09.line: move gently through the world today.
09-09.meaning: like Guru Har Rai Sahib Ji and the flower, notice the small lives around you.

09-10.title: Freedom of Faith
09-10.line: Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji gave his life for others' right to their own faith.
09-10.meaning: he stood up for people who weren't Sikhs. he is called "Hind di Chadar", shield of India.

09-11.title: Pauri 26
09-11.line: priceless are the virtues, and priceless those who trade in them.
09-11.meaning: goodness is the real wealth. you can deal in it today.

09-12.title: Those Who Shared
09-12.line: remember those who remembered the Name and shared their food.
09-12.meaning: Ardas recalls Sikhs who served and shared. their example is part of every prayer.

09-13.title: Miri and Piri
09-13.line: worldly duty and spiritual life, together.
09-13.meaning: Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji taught that faith and everyday responsibility belong side by side.

09-14.title: Bhana
09-14.meaning: sweetly accepting what we can't change, while doing what we can.

09-15.title: Bhagat Sadhna Ji
09-15.meaning: Sadhna Ji's hymn shows that no one is too far from grace.

09-16.title: Bhai Daya Singh
09-16.line: Bhai Daya Singh Ji was the first to step forward in 1699.
09-16.meaning: the first of the Panj Pyare. courage is often just being first to say yes.

09-17.title: Golden Arrows
09-17.line: Guru Gobind Singh Ji's arrows were tipped with gold, tradition says.
09-17.meaning: so that anyone wounded could pay for care. kindness, even toward opponents.

09-18.title: Simple Ardas
09-18.line: say a short prayer for someone who is struggling.
09-18.meaning: Ardas asks good for all. one name is enough.

09-19.title: Guru Granth Sahib
09-19.meaning: Sikhs bow to the Guru Granth Sahib as their Guru. its words guide every part of life.

09-20.title: Anandpur
09-20.line: Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji founded Anandpur, the city of bliss.
09-20.meaning: later the Khalsa was born there.

09-21.title: Farid: Your Own Book
09-21.line: if you are wise, don't write black marks against others.
09-21.meaning: Baba Farid Ji asks us to look at our own heart first.

09-22.title: Honest Money
09-22.line: make sure your earnings today are fair and honest.
09-22.meaning: Guru Nanak Dev Ji chose honest bread over rich feasts.

09-23.title: Gurdwara Bangla Sahib
09-23.line: where Guru Har Krishan Sahib Ji cared for the sick.
09-23.meaning: in Delhi, its langar serves thousands every day.

09-24.title: So Dar
09-24.line: the winds, the waters and the fires all sing Your praise.
09-24.meaning: pauri 27 pictures all creation singing. listen to the wind today.

09-25.title: Mukti
09-25.meaning: freedom from ego and fear, found while living, not only after.

09-26.title: Gurmukhi
09-26.line: the script of the Guru's word.
09-26.meaning: Guru Angad Dev Ji shaped the Gurmukhi script so everyone could read the Guru's teachings.

09-27.title: Clean Up
09-27.line: tidy a shared space without being asked.
09-27.meaning: like seva at the gurdwara, caring for shared spaces is caring for people.

09-28.title: Bhai Dharam Singh
09-28.line: Bhai Dharam Singh Ji came from a farming family.
09-28.meaning: the second of the Panj Pyare. the Khalsa welcomed all backgrounds.

09-29.title: The Khalsa
09-29.line: in 1699 Guru Gobind Singh Ji created the Khalsa.
09-29.meaning: five volunteers stepped forward, and a fearless, giving community began.

09-30.title: Pauri 28
09-30.line: conquer your own mind, and you conquer the world.
09-30.meaning: the real victory is inside. one calm response today is a win.

10-01.title: Raag
10-01.line: the Guru's word is set to music.
10-01.meaning: most of the Guru Granth Sahib is arranged by raag, musical modes for different moods.

10-02.title: Anand
10-02.line: joy has come, mother, for i have found the True Guru.
10-02.meaning: the opening of Anand Sahib by Guru Amar Das Ji, sung at every celebration.

10-03.title: Joyful Faith
10-03.line: let your faith be joyful today.
10-03.meaning: Anand Sahib sings of bliss. Sikhi is meant to bring joy.

10-04.title: Anand
10-04.meaning: deep joy that comes from closeness to the Guru.

10-05.title: Sukhmani Sahib
10-05.meaning: Guru Arjan Dev Ji's long bani, read by many for calm in hard times.

10-06.title: Honest Word
10-06.meaning: Gurbani says truthful living is higher than truth itself.

10-07.title: Waheguru
10-07.meaning: the Sikh word for God expresses awe. say it slowly, once, with wonder.

10-08.title: Bhagat Ramanand Ji
10-08.meaning: Ramanand Ji's hymn says the divine is within, not only at pilgrim places.

10-09.title: Pauri 29
10-09.line: let spiritual wisdom be your food, and compassion its server.
10-09.meaning: feed your heart with wisdom, and let kindness hand it out.

10-10.title: The Guru Becomes the Disciple
10-10.line: Guru Gobind Singh Ji took amrit from the Panj Pyare.
10-10.meaning: the Guru bowed to his own Sikhs. "wonderful is the Guru who is also a disciple."

10-11.title: Bhai Himmat Singh
10-11.line: Bhai Himmat Singh Ji came from far away to answer the call.
10-11.meaning: one of the Panj Pyare, from the Jagannath Puri region. faith gathered people from everywhere.

10-12.title: Anand Sahib
10-12.meaning: Guru Amar Das Ji's bani is sung at celebrations and at the close of services.

10-13.title: Gurdwara Sis Ganj Sahib
10-13.line: in Delhi, where Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji was martyred.
10-13.meaning: a place to honor the right of all to their own faith.

10-14.title: Lavan
10-14.line: in the first round, the Creator shows the way of married life.
10-14.meaning: Guru Ram Das Ji's four lavan are sung at every Sikh wedding. love, rooted in the Guru.

10-15.title: Fearless
10-15.meaning: the Mool Mantar says the Creator is fearless. a little of that lives in you.

10-16.title: Vismaad
10-16.meaning: the feeling Guru Nanak Dev Ji had looking at creation. look up at the sky today.

10-17.title: Rest in Hukam
10-17.line: what can you accept today, just as it is?
10-17.meaning: trusting hukam brings peace in the middle of change.

10-18.title: Herbs for an Opponent's Son
10-18.line: Guru Har Rai Sahib Ji sent rare herbs to heal the emperor's son.
10-18.meaning: though his family had been treated badly, he healed anyway. the Guru's house helps all.

10-19.title: Langar Seva
10-19.meaning: anyone can help in the langar kitchen. many friendships begin over a pile of onions.

10-20.title: Pauri 32
10-20.line: if my one tongue became a hundred thousand, i'd still repeat Your Name.
10-20.meaning: love for Waheguru never runs out of words.

10-21.title: The Poet Guru
10-21.line: Guru Gobind Singh Ji wrote poetry in many languages.
10-21.meaning: he kept 52 poets at his court. words and courage together.

10-22.title: Kirat
10-22.meaning: a farmer, a nurse, a student: honest effort is worship in Sikhi.

10-23.title: Bhai Mohkam Singh
10-23.line: Bhai Mohkam Singh Ji, a tailor, stepped forward in 1699.
10-23.meaning: one of the Panj Pyare. ordinary people became beloved ones.

10-24.title: Shabad for the Day
10-24.meaning: kirtan can live in the kitchen and the car, not just the gurdwara.

10-25.title: Kirpa
10-25.meaning: the Creator's kindness, which we can pass on to others.

10-26.title: Why Search the Forests?
10-26.line: why go searching in the forests? the Lord is with you.
10-26.meaning: Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji says Waheguru lives within, like fragrance in a flower.

10-27.title: Without Hate
10-27.meaning: nirvair, without hate, is how the Mool Mantar describes the Creator.

10-28.title: Pauri 33
10-28.line: no power to speak or stay silent: everything rests in grace.
10-28.meaning: a humbling pauri. we don't run everything, and that's a relief.

10-29.title: Simran on the Go
10-29.meaning: simran can travel with you: on a walk, on a bus, while you cook.

10-30.title: Guru Granth, Forever
10-30.line: Guru Gobind Singh Ji named the Guru Granth Sahib the eternal Guru.
10-30.meaning: in 1708 the line of human Gurus became the living word.

10-31.title: Sat Sri Akal
10-31.line: Sat Sri Akal: true is the Timeless One.
10-31.meaning: the everyday Sikh greeting. every hello is a small reminder of the eternal.

11-01.title: The Bhatts
11-01.meaning: the Bhatts' swaiye in the Guru Granth Sahib sing the Gurus' greatness.

11-02.title: Share Your Skill
11-02.meaning: sharing isn't only food; it's skills and time too.

11-03.title: Gurbani Before Sleep
11-03.line: end the day with the Guru's word.
11-03.meaning: a few lines of Kirtan Sohila can help the day close in peace.

11-04.title: Pauri 34
11-04.line: amid nights, days and seasons, the earth was made a place for dharma.
11-04.meaning: the whole planet is a dharamsal, a place to practice goodness. including your street.

11-05.title: Dharam
11-05.meaning: doing what is right, honest and fair, every day.

11-06.title: Fatehgarh Sahib
11-06.line: where the younger Sahibzade are remembered.
11-06.meaning: the Shaheedi Jor Mela in December fills it with sangat.

11-07.title: Bhai Sahib Singh
11-07.line: Bhai Sahib Singh Ji, a barber, offered himself in 1699.
11-07.meaning: the fifth of the Panj Pyare. in the Khalsa, no work is lowly.

11-08.title: Shared by All
11-08.line: all share in Your grace; You are excluded from no one.
11-08.meaning: Guru Arjan Dev Ji: everyone is part of the Creator's family.

11-09.title: Listen to Kirtan
11-09.line: play kirtan while you cook or travel.
11-09.meaning: let the Guru's word fill the room.

11-10.title: Guru Nanak's Childhood
11-10.line: young Nanak asked his teacher deep questions.
11-10.meaning: even as a boy he wanted to understand the real meaning of things. curiosity is sacred.

11-11.title: Visiting the Sick
11-11.line: sit with someone who is unwell.
11-11.meaning: Sikh history is full of care for the sick. a call or a visit is seva.

11-12.title: Watch the Thieves
11-12.line: notice which of the five thieves visits you today.
11-12.meaning: lust, anger, greed, attachment, pride. naming them takes away their power.

11-13.title: Gian Khand
11-13.line: in the realm of knowledge, wisdom shines bright.
11-13.meaning: Japji Sahib describes stages of the spiritual journey. understanding is one bright step.

11-14.title: Water Seva
11-14.meaning: a simple, ancient seva. Bhai Kanhaiya Ji gave water to all.

11-15.title: Sarbat
11-15.meaning: Sikh prayers are for everyone. no one is left out.

11-16.title: The Letter of Victory
11-16.line: Guru Gobind Singh Ji answered cruelty with a letter about truth.
11-16.meaning: the Zafarnama, "letter of victory", calls an emperor to keep his word. words can be brave.

11-17.title: Mata Sulakhni
11-17.line: Mata Sulakhni Ji held the family together during the Guru's long travels.
11-17.meaning: quiet steadiness at home is its own kind of seva.

11-18.title: Bhai Sangat Singh
11-18.line: Bhai Sangat Singh Ji stayed behind at Chamkaur.
11-18.meaning: a loyal Sikh remembered for selfless courage.

11-19.title: Only the Creator
11-19.line: everyone makes mistakes; only the Guru and Creator do not.
11-19.meaning: Guru Nanak Dev Ji makes room for our mistakes. forgive yours, and others'.

11-20.title: Share Credit
11-20.line: thank the people who helped you succeed.
11-20.meaning: nothing is done alone. the Guru's grace works through many hands.

11-21.title: Matha Tekna
11-21.meaning: touching the forehead to the floor before the Guru Granth Sahib is a sign of humility.

11-22.title: Visit the Gurdwara
11-22.line: visit a gurdwara this week, or listen to kirtan online.
11-22.meaning: the door is always open, and langar is always warm.

11-23.title: Saram Khand
11-23.line: in the realm of effort, the mind is shaped with beauty.
11-23.meaning: effort and humility polish us, like a craftsperson shaping fine work.

11-24.title: The Khalsa Greeting
11-24.line: the Khalsa belongs to Waheguru; victory belongs to Waheguru.
11-24.meaning: "Waheguru Ji Ka Khalsa, Waheguru Ji Ki Fateh": a greeting that hands all credit to God.

11-25.title: Parkarma
11-25.meaning: at the Harmandir Sahib, pilgrims walk the marble path around the sarovar, often in silence.

11-26.title: Akal
11-26.meaning: Waheguru is beyond time. even on rushed days, the eternal is close.

11-27.title: Satta and Balwand
11-27.line: two musicians whose ballad is in the Guru.
11-27.meaning: their vaar in Raag Ramkali tells how the light passed from Guru to Guru.

11-28.title: Bebe Nanaki
11-28.line: Bebe Nanaki Ji was the first to see her brother's light.
11-28.meaning: Guru Nanak Dev Ji's older sister believed in him from the start. thank someone who believed in you.

11-29.title: Hemkunt Sahib
11-29.line: a gurdwara high in the Himalayas beside a lake.
11-29.meaning: pilgrims climb for hours each summer. reaching it is itself a prayer.

11-30.title: Cover Your Head
11-30.line: cover your head while you read Gurbani today.
11-30.meaning: a small sign of respect that helps the mind settle.

12-01.title: Mata Jito
12-01.line: Mata Jito Ji was a wife of Guru Gobind Singh Ji.
12-01.meaning: remembered as a loving mother to her sons and the sangat.

12-02.title: Sach Khand
12-02.line: in the realm of truth dwells the Formless One.
12-02.meaning: the journey's end in Japji Sahib: the home of truth, reached by grace.

12-03.title: Sarovar
12-03.line: a sacred pool beside the gurdwara.
12-03.meaning: many gurdwaras have a sarovar where pilgrims bathe and reflect.

12-04.title: With the Lowly
12-04.line: Nanak walks with the lowest of the low.
12-04.meaning: Guru Nanak Dev Ji chose to stand with the humble, not the proud.

12-05.title: Remember the Gurus
12-05.line: think of one of the ten Gurus and what they taught.
12-05.meaning: each Guru shows a different side of the same light.

12-06.title: Nirbhau
12-06.meaning: from the Mool Mantar: the Creator is fearless, and invites us to be too.

12-07.title: Gurpurab
12-07.meaning: gurpurabs are marked with Akhand Path, kirtan, langar and processions.

12-08.title: Bibi Bhani
12-08.line: Bibi Bhani Ji served her father, Guru Amar Das Ji, with deep love.
12-08.meaning: she was mother of Guru Arjan Dev Ji. her seva is remembered with honor.

12-09.title: Elders
12-09.line: call an elder in your family today.
12-09.meaning: Sikh history honors grandparents like Mata Gujri Ji. their stories matter.

12-10.title: Pauri 38
12-10.line: let patience be the goldsmith and love the melting pot.
12-10.meaning: Guru Nanak Dev Ji's picture of a life well made: self-control, patience, wisdom, love.

12-11.title: Nagar Kirtan
12-11.meaning: processions led by the Panj Pyare carry kirtan out into the community, with free food for all.

12-12.title: Bhai Dyala
12-12.line: Bhai Dyala Ji kept reciting Japji Sahib to the end.
12-12.meaning: he stood with Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji in Delhi, calm in prayer.

12-13.title: Body and Universe
12-13.line: what is in the universe is in the body too.
12-13.meaning: Bhagat Pipa Ji: everything you seek outside is also within you.

12-14.title: Care for Creation
12-14.meaning: Gurbani calls air, water and earth our family. treat them kindly.

12-15.title: Nirvair
12-15.meaning: from the Mool Mantar: the Creator holds no hate. we can let go of ours.

12-16.title: The Thread That Doesn't Break
12-16.line: make compassion the cotton and contentment the thread.
12-16.meaning: Guru Nanak Dev Ji asked for a sacred thread made of virtues, one that never wears out.

12-17.title: Mata Gujri
12-17.line: Mata Gujri Ji raised her grandsons with courage and faith.
12-17.meaning: a grandmother whose strength the Sikh world still honors.

12-18.title: Sangrand
12-18.line: the first day of each month.
12-18.meaning: many Sikhs visit the gurdwara on sangrand, when the month's Barah Maha is read.

12-19.title: Children
12-19.line: tell a child a story about the Gurus.
12-19.meaning: the Sakhis, the stories of the Gurus, are how Sikhi passes on.

12-20.title: Air, Water, Earth
12-20.original: ਪਵਣੁ ਗੁਰੂ ਪਾਣੀ ਪਿਤਾ ਮਾਤਾ ਧਰਤਿ ਮਹਤੁ ॥
12-20.line: air is the guru, water the father, earth the great mother.
12-20.meaning: the closing salok of Japji Sahib honors nature as family. treat it gently today.

12-21.title: Ik Onkar
12-21.meaning: the first words of the Guru Granth Sahib, with the numeral one: one Creator, in everything.

12-22.title: Baba Sundar Ji
12-22.line: a great-grandson of Guru Amar Das Ji.
12-22.meaning: his "Sadd" tells of the Guru's last words: don't weep, sing God's praise.

12-23.title: Paonta Sahib
12-23.line: where Guru Gobind Singh Ji wrote poetry by the river.
12-23.meaning: a peaceful riverside town in the hills.

12-24.title: Barah Maha
12-24.line: a song for each of the twelve months.
12-24.meaning: Guru Nanak Dev Ji and Guru Arjan Dev Ji wrote of the soul's longing through the seasons.

12-25.title: Bhai Sati Das
12-25.line: Bhai Sati Das Ji remained peaceful in faith.
12-25.meaning: one of three Sikhs who stood beside Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji, remembered with deep honor.

12-26.title: A Prayer
12-26.line: my Master, to You i pray.
12-26.meaning: Guru Arjan Dev Ji in Sukhmani Sahib: body and soul are Your gift. the start of Sikh prayer.

12-27.title: Hope
12-27.line: whatever happened yesterday, today can be good.

12-28.title: Gur Prasad
12-28.line: gur prasad: by the Guru's grace.
12-28.meaning: the last words of the Mool Mantar. everything good comes by grace.

12-29.title: Mata Sahib Kaur
12-29.line: Mata Sahib Kaur Ji added sweetness to the first amrit.
12-29.meaning: she is honored as the mother of the Khalsa.

12-30.title: Neighbors
12-30.line: do something kind for a neighbor.
12-30.meaning: the sangat includes the people next door.

12-31.title: Faces Radiant
12-31.line: those who remember the Name shine, and many are freed with them.
12-31.meaning: the last line of Japji Sahib: our practice blesses others too.

2026-10-27.title: Prakash Purab, Guru Ram Das Ji
2026-10-27.line: happy gurpurab of Guru Ram Das Ji, founder of Amritsar.
2026-10-27.meaning: the fourth Guru wrote the lavan sung at every Sikh wedding and built the city around the sacred pool. (date may vary)

2026-11-08.title: Bandi Chhor Divas
2026-11-08.line: freedom shared: no one walks out alone.
2026-11-08.meaning: Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji left prison only when 52 kings could leave with him. Sikhs light the Harmandir Sahib and their homes tonight.

2026-11-11.title: Gurta Gaddi Divas
2026-11-11.line: the word became the Guru, forever.
2026-11-11.meaning: Sikhs remember Guru Gobind Singh Ji naming the Guru Granth Sahib the eternal Guru in 1708. (date may vary)

2026-11-15.title: Baba Deep Singh Ji
2026-11-15.line: a scholar who gave everything for the Guru's house.
2026-11-15.meaning: Baba Deep Singh Ji copied the Guru Granth Sahib by hand and is remembered for his devotion to the Harmandir Sahib. (date may vary)

2026-11-24.title: Guru Nanak Gurpurab
2026-11-24.line: happy Prakash Purab of Guru Nanak Dev Ji.
2026-11-24.meaning: the founder of Sikhi taught one Creator, honest work, sharing and remembering God. gurdwaras glow with lights, kirtan and langar.

2026-12-13.title: Bhai Mati Das, Sati Das and Dyala Ji
2026-12-13.line: three Sikhs who stayed calm in prayer to the end.
2026-12-13.meaning: they stood beside Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji in Delhi in 1675. Sikhs remember their peace and courage. (date may vary)

2026-12-14.title: Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji
2026-12-14.line: remembering the Guru who protected others' freedom of faith.
2026-12-14.meaning: the ninth Guru gave his life in 1675 for people's right to their own beliefs. many read his saloks today. the Nanakshahi calendar marks it on 24 November. (date may vary)

2026-12-21.title: Leaving Anandpur
2026-12-21.line: the week of remembering the Sahibzade begins.
2026-12-21.meaning: Sikhs remember Guru Gobind Singh Ji's family leaving Anandpur in December 1704, and the sacrifices that followed. (date may vary)

2026-12-23.title: Saka Chamkaur Sahib
2026-12-23.line: the elder Sahibzade, remembered for their courage.
2026-12-23.meaning: Sahibzada Ajit Singh Ji and Sahibzada Jujhar Singh Ji stood bravely at Chamkaur. a day for quiet prayer. (date may vary)

2026-12-28.title: The Younger Sahibzade and Mata Gujri Ji
2026-12-28.line: two small boys and their grandmother held to their faith.
2026-12-28.meaning: Sahibzada Zorawar Singh Ji, Sahibzada Fateh Singh Ji and Mata Gujri Ji are remembered at Fatehgarh Sahib. many sangats mark it a day or two earlier. (date may vary)

2027-01-14.title: Maghi
2027-01-14.line: the forty who returned were forgiven.
2027-01-14.meaning: at Muktsar, Guru Gobind Singh Ji blessed forty Sikhs who came back. Maghi celebrates second chances. (date may vary)

2027-01-15.title: Guru Gobind Singh Ji Gurpurab
2027-01-15.line: happy Prakash Purab of Guru Gobind Singh Ji.
2027-01-15.meaning: the tenth Guru, poet and founder of the Khalsa. gurdwaras hold kirtan and langar. some calendars mark it on 5 January. (date may vary)

2027-02-20.title: Bhagat Ravidas Ji
2027-02-20.line: a city with no sorrow and no ranks.
2027-02-20.meaning: Bhagat Ravidas Ji's hymns in the Guru Granth Sahib dream of Begampura, where everyone is equal. (date may vary)

2027-02-26.title: Guru Har Rai Sahib Ji
2027-02-26.line: happy gurpurab of the gentle, healing Guru.
2027-02-26.meaning: the seventh Guru kept gardens, cared for animals and gave medicine to anyone in need. (date may vary)

2027-03-14.title: Nanakshahi New Year
2027-03-14.line: a new year begins on the first of Chet.
2027-03-14.meaning: the Nanakshahi year starts today. a fresh page: begin it with Ardas.

2027-03-23.title: Hola Mohalla
2027-03-23.line: the day after Holi, Sikhs gather for courage and joy.
2027-03-23.meaning: Guru Gobind Singh Ji began Hola Mohalla at Anandpur Sahib: kirtan, poetry, gatka and huge langars. (date may vary)

2027-04-14.title: Vaisakhi
2027-04-14.line: happy Vaisakhi: the Khalsa was born on this day in 1699.
2027-04-14.meaning: Guru Gobind Singh Ji created the Khalsa at Anandpur Sahib. it's also Punjab's harvest festival, full of nagar kirtans and langar. (date may vary)

2027-06-18.title: Guru Arjan Dev Ji
2027-06-18.line: remembering the first Sikh martyr, who said "Your will is sweet".
2027-06-18.meaning: Guru Arjan Dev Ji compiled the Guru Granth Sahib and built the Harmandir Sahib. many serve cold sweet drinks, chhabeel, to passers-by today. (date may vary)

2027-10-29.title: Bandi Chhor Divas
2027-10-29.line: the Guru wouldn't leave until everyone could leave.
2027-10-29.meaning: Sikhs remember Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji freeing 52 kings, and light lamps at home and at the Harmandir Sahib.

2027-10-31.title: Gurta Gaddi Divas
2027-10-31.line: the Guru Granth Sahib: our living Guru.
2027-10-31.meaning: Sikhs mark the day Guru Gobind Singh Ji passed the Guruship to the Guru Granth Sahib. (date may vary)

2027-11-14.title: Guru Nanak Gurpurab
2027-11-14.line: happy Prakash Purab of Guru Nanak Dev Ji: there is One.
2027-11-14.meaning: gurdwaras celebrate with Akhand Path, kirtan, lights and langar for all. share something sweet today.

2027-11-24.title: Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji
2027-11-24.line: the Guru who stood for everyone's freedom of faith.
2027-11-24.meaning: marked on 24 November in the Nanakshahi calendar; many gurdwaras follow a lunar date, so check yours. (date may vary)

2027-12-23.title: Saka Chamkaur Sahib
2027-12-23.line: brave hearts at Chamkaur, never forgotten.
2027-12-23.meaning: Sikhs remember the elder Sahibzade and the Sikhs who stood with Guru Gobind Singh Ji at Chamkaur. (date may vary)

2027-12-28.title: The Younger Sahibzade and Mata Gujri Ji
2027-12-28.line: faith that was bigger than fear, in two small hearts.
2027-12-28.meaning: Sikhs gather at Fatehgarh Sahib and gurdwaras everywhere to remember them. many mark it a day or two earlier. (date may vary)
